quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Three years ago, the local newspaper was losing readers, so its editors decided to change their approach. They stopped printing daily and instead published a longer edition on Saturdays, with detailed reports and interviews. A new website now carries the breaking news throughout the week. Subscriptions have risen steadily since the change, and the editors say the paper is finally profitable again. The editors also plan to hire two more reporters next year.
quests.question: The newspaper's finances improved after it reduced how often it prints.
quests.hint: Compare the situation before the change with the situation now.
quests.explanation: Printing only on Saturdays came first, and afterward subscriptions rose and the paper became profitable.
quests.evidenceLine: Subscriptions have risen steadily since the change, and the editors say the paper is finally profitable again.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Rosalind's father moved to Argentina in 1985 to work on a farm. He met her mother there two years later, and they married in 1990. Rosalind was born in 1993, the youngest of three children. She now lives in Spain, but she visits her parents every year. Every Sunday the whole family still eats lunch together.
quests.question: Rosalind's parents met in Argentina.
quests.hint: Follow where her father lived when he met her mother.
quests.explanation: He met her mother "there," which refers to Argentina, where he had moved.
quests.evidenceLine: He met her mother there two years later, and they married in 1990.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Doctors often ask patients about their sleep because poor sleep is linked to many health problems. People who regularly sleep too little are more likely to catch colds, gain weight, and feel low. However, sleeping much more than nine hours can also be a sign of illness. The best approach is to find the amount of sleep that leaves you rested. Adults who sleep well also tend to make fewer mistakes at work.
quests.question: Sleeping far more than nine hours a night can point to a health problem.
quests.hint: Focus on the contrast introduced in the third sentence.
quests.explanation: The third sentence says very long sleep can also be a sign of illness.
quests.evidenceLine: However, sleeping much more than nine hours can also be a sign of illness.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Olive oil can be labeled "extra virgin" only if it is made by pressing olives without heat or chemicals. It has a stronger flavor than refined oil, and many cooks use it mainly for salads and finishing dishes. For frying at high temperatures, cheaper oils are often preferred because they do not burn as easily. Extra virgin oil should be kept in a dark bottle, away from light. Prices are usually higher than for other kinds of oil.
quests.question: Extra virgin olive oil is produced with the help of chemicals.
quests.hint: Read the conditions for the "extra virgin" label.
quests.explanation: The label requires pressing without heat or chemicals, so chemicals are excluded.
quests.evidenceLine: Olive oil can be labeled "extra virgin" only if it is made by pressing olives without heat or chemicals.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: A tornado forms when a rotating column of air stretches from a storm cloud to the ground. Most tornadoes last only a few minutes, but the strongest can stay on the ground for more than an hour. Wind speeds inside can exceed three hundred kilometers per hour. Because they are so unpredictable, warnings usually come only ten to fifteen minutes before a tornado arrives. Storm chasers study them from a safe distance using special cameras.
quests.question: Tornadoes typically last longer than an hour.
quests.hint: Separate what is typical from what is rare.
quests.explanation: Most last only a few minutes. Lasting over an hour applies to the strongest ones only.
quests.evidenceLine: Most tornadoes last only a few minutes, but the strongest can stay on the ground for more than an hour.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria, but they do not work against viruses. A cold or the flu is caused by a virus, so taking antibiotics for these illnesses will not help. Using them when they are not needed also contributes to the problem of resistant bacteria. Doctors therefore prescribe them only when a bacterial infection is likely. Many patients ask for them anyway, but doctors try to explain the risks.
quests.question: Colds are caused by viruses, so antibiotics are the wrong treatment.
quests.hint: Ask what causes a cold and what antibiotics target.
quests.explanation: A cold is caused by a virus, and antibiotics do not work against viruses.
quests.evidenceLine: A cold or the flu is caused by a virus, so taking antibiotics for these illnesses will not help.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: The mayor announced that the old railway bridge will be turned into a pedestrian park. The bridge has not carried trains for thirty years and was expected to be demolished. Engineers found that its steel structure was still strong, so preserving it would cost less than tearing it down. Work is scheduled to begin in spring. Local residents will be invited to suggest names for the new park.
quests.question: Keeping the bridge is cheaper than demolishing it.
quests.hint: Look for the engineers' cost comparison.
quests.explanation: Preserving the strong structure would cost less than tearing it down.
quests.evidenceLine: Engineers found that its steel structure was still strong, so preserving it would cost less than tearing it down.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Artificial intelligence programs learn by studying huge numbers of examples. A program that translates languages, for instance, may be trained on millions of sentences that have already been translated by people. The more good examples it sees, the better its results usually become. However, a program can make mistakes if the examples it learned from contained errors. Engineers therefore spend much of their time cleaning and checking the data.
quests.question: Fewer examples usually lead to better results.
quests.hint: Think about the link between examples and quality.
quests.explanation: The passage says more good examples usually improve results, not fewer.
quests.evidenceLine: The more good examples it sees, the better its results usually become.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: When Nadine and Marcus opened their small bicycle repair shop, they expected to earn most of their money from repairs. Instead, they found that customers were buying more accessories, such as lights and locks. Within a year, accessories accounted for sixty percent of their income. They now spend more time choosing products than fixing bicycles. Their first customers were mostly students from a nearby university.
quests.question: Most of the shop's income comes from repairs.
quests.hint: Compare the two sources of income after one year.
quests.explanation: Accessories provide sixty percent, so repairs bring in less than half.
quests.evidenceLine: Within a year, accessories accounted for sixty percent of their income.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Suresh has been a bus driver for fifteen years. He says that the hardest part of the job is not the traffic but keeping calm when passengers are angry. Over time, he has learned to listen quietly and then explain the problem simply. His supervisor says that Suresh receives fewer complaints than any other driver on his route. Passengers often greet him by name when they board.
quests.question: Suresh finds heavy traffic the most difficult part of his job.
quests.hint: Whose opinion is being reported, and what does he say?
quests.explanation: He says the hardest part is not the traffic but staying calm with angry passengers.
quests.evidenceLine: He says that the hardest part of the job is not the traffic but keeping calm when passengers are angry.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Some words have no exact equivalent in other languages. The Portuguese word "saudade" describes a deep, gentle longing for someone or something that is absent. Translators often need a whole sentence to explain it. Speakers of the language, however, use it easily in everyday conversation. Language learners often list such words as their favorites.
quests.question: Translating saudade usually takes more than one word.
quests.hint: Focus on what translators need.
quests.explanation: Translators often need a whole sentence, which is more than a single word.
quests.evidenceLine: Translators often need a whole sentence to explain it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Wetlands act like natural sponges, soaking up water during heavy rain and releasing it slowly afterward. When towns drain wetlands to build houses, floods often become more severe downstream. Several cities have now begun to restore wetlands instead of building concrete barriers. The approach is cheaper and also creates a home for birds and fish. Environmental groups have welcomed the change in approach.
quests.question: Draining wetlands can make flooding worse.
quests.hint: Read what happens when towns drain wetlands.
quests.explanation: Floods often become more severe downstream after wetlands are drained.
quests.evidenceLine: When towns drain wetlands to build houses, floods often become more severe downstream.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Migrating birds can travel thousands of kilometers each year between their breeding and wintering areas. The Arctic tern makes the longest journey, flying from the Arctic to Antarctica and back. Scientists have found that some birds navigate by using the Earth's magnetic field, along with the position of the sun and stars. Young birds often travel with experienced adults. Researchers attach tiny trackers to the birds to follow their routes.
quests.question: The Arctic tern's yearly journey is shorter than that of most other migrating birds.
quests.hint: Find how the tern compares with other migrants.
quests.explanation: The tern makes the longest journey, so its trip is not shorter than most.
quests.evidenceLine: The Arctic tern makes the longest journey, flying from the Arctic to Antarctica and back.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: In many Indian homes, guests are offered tea or water as soon as they arrive. Refusing it may seem impolite, so visitors often accept at least a small cup. The host will usually insist a little, even when the guest says no. This behavior shows care rather than pressure. Visitors from other countries are often surprised by this kindness.
quests.question: A host may offer a drink more than once after a guest declines.
quests.hint: Look at what the host does after a refusal.
quests.explanation: The host usually insists a little even when the guest says no.
quests.evidenceLine: The host will usually insist a little, even when the guest says no.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: The documentary follows three young chess players preparing for a national championship. Although the subject sounds narrow, the film focuses on friendship and pressure rather than on the game itself. Viewers who know nothing about chess are therefore just as likely to enjoy it. The film won an audience prize at a small festival last year. The director spent four years filming the players and their families.
quests.question: Viewers who are new to chess can enjoy the documentary as much as fans.
quests.hint: Look at what the film focuses on.
quests.explanation: The film is about friendship and pressure, so people who know nothing about chess are just as likely to enjoy it.
quests.evidenceLine: Viewers who know nothing about chess are therefore just as likely to enjoy it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Regular stretching improves flexibility, but it does not prevent every injury. Studies show that warming up with light movement before exercise is more useful than stretching cold muscles. People who sit at desks for long periods, however, benefit from stretching during the day. Even two minutes every hour can reduce stiffness in the back and neck. Physical therapists say that gentle movement is better than long rest.
quests.question: Warming up is more useful than stretching cold muscles.
quests.hint: Compare the two pre-exercise habits.
quests.explanation: The studies show light movement is more useful than stretching cold muscles.
quests.evidenceLine: Studies show that warming up with light movement before exercise is more useful than stretching cold muscles.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Most of the mass of an atom is concentrated in its tiny nucleus. The electrons that surround the nucleus are much lighter, and they move at great speed. If an atom were the size of a football stadium, the nucleus would be about the size of a pea. Most of the atom is therefore empty space. Physicists use large machines to study these tiny particles.
quests.question: Electrons make up most of an atom's mass.
quests.hint: Which part of the atom is heavy?
quests.explanation: The nucleus holds most of the mass, and electrons are much lighter.
quests.evidenceLine: Most of the mass of an atom is concentrated in its tiny nucleus. The electrons that surround the nucleus are much lighter, and they move at great speed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Maria's company allows employees to work from home two days a week. Most staff choose Tuesdays and Thursdays, because those are the days when there are the fewest meetings. On Mondays and Fridays, the office is usually full. Managers say that productivity has not changed since the policy started. Some employees say they save an hour of travel on those days.
quests.question: Employees at Maria's company must come to the office five days a week.
quests.hint: Read what the company allows.
quests.explanation: Two days a week may be worked from home, so five office days are not required.
quests.evidenceLine: Maria's company allows employees to work from home two days a week.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Password managers store all of a person's passwords in one encrypted place. The user needs to remember only one strong master password to unlock the rest. Security experts recommend them because most people otherwise reuse simple passwords across many sites. If the master password is forgotten, the company usually cannot recover it. Most of them also warn users when a password is too weak.
quests.question: Users can easily recover a forgotten master password through the company.
quests.hint: Consider the result of losing the master password.
quests.explanation: The company usually cannot recover it, so recovery is not easy.
quests.evidenceLine: If the master password is forgotten, the company usually cannot recover it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Moss has no true roots. It absorbs water directly through its leaves and uses tiny threads to hold on to rocks or trees. Because it needs constant moisture, it grows best in shady, damp places. Some types can dry out completely and then revive within hours when rain returns. Gardeners sometimes use it to cover the ground in shady corners.
quests.question: Some types of moss can recover after drying out completely.
quests.hint: Look at what happens when rain returns.
quests.explanation: Some types revive within hours of rain after drying out.
quests.evidenceLine: Some types can dry out completely and then revive within hours when rain returns.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: When Tomas bought his house, the kitchen was dark and old. He replaced the cabinets and painted the walls white, but he kept the original tile floor because it was in good condition. The renovation took six weeks, two weeks longer than the contractor had promised. Tomas says he would do it again, although the noise was tiring. The new lights above the counter were his favorite change.
quests.question: The renovation finished sooner than the contractor had promised.
quests.hint: Compare the actual time with the promised time.
quests.explanation: It took six weeks, which was two weeks longer than promised.
quests.evidenceLine: The renovation took six weeks, two weeks longer than the contractor had promised.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Children under the age of thirteen should sit in the back seat of a car whenever possible. Airbags are designed for adults and can injure small bodies when they open at high speed. Younger children also need a car seat that fits their weight and height. A seat belt alone does not protect them properly. Some countries also have laws that set a minimum age for front seat travel.
quests.question: An airbag can be dangerous for a small child.
quests.hint: Find the reason for the back-seat advice.
quests.explanation: Airbags are designed for adults and can injure small bodies.
quests.evidenceLine: Airbags are designed for adults and can injure small bodies when they open at high speed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: When people learn a second language, they often translate every word in their head. With practice, this habit fades, and they begin to think directly in the new language. Teachers encourage learners to study phrases instead of single words, because phrases are easier to use naturally. Learners who read for pleasure make especially fast progress. Language apps now use short phrases in many of their lessons.
quests.question: Teachers say learners should memorize single words rather than phrases.
quests.hint: Notice the teachers' encouragement.
quests.explanation: Teachers encourage studying phrases instead of single words.
quests.evidenceLine: Teachers encourage learners to study phrases instead of single words, because phrases are easier to use naturally.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: The theater company rehearsed the new play for two months before the first show. On opening night, the lead actor became ill and his understudy took over with only a few hours' notice. Although he made a few small mistakes, the audience applauded warmly. The company decided to keep the understudy in the role for the rest of the week. The reviews in the local newspaper were generous to the whole cast.
quests.question: The audience did not applaud the understudy.
quests.hint: Read how the audience responded.
quests.explanation: The audience applauded warmly despite a few small mistakes.
quests.evidenceLine: Although he made a few small mistakes, the audience applauded warmly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Travelers who fly across several time zones often suffer from jet lag. The body's internal clock needs time to adjust, so people may feel tired during the day and awake at night. Doctors suggest spending time in daylight at the new destination to help the clock adjust. Most people recover after about one day for each time zone crossed. Traveling east is usually said to be harder than traveling west.
quests.question: Most people need about four days to recover after crossing four time zones.
quests.hint: Apply the rule in the fourth sentence.
quests.explanation: One day per time zone crossed makes four days for four zones.
quests.evidenceLine: Most people recover after about one day for each time zone crossed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: The family dinner at Anwar's house has a rule: no phones at the table. Everyone puts their devices in a basket by the door before sitting down. Anwar's younger sister complained at first, but she now says that conversations are more interesting. Even their grandfather, who rarely uses a phone, agrees that the rule is a good one. The basket has been in the hallway for more than a year now.
quests.question: Anwar's sister has changed her opinion about the phone rule.
quests.hint: Compare her first reaction with her view now.
quests.explanation: She complained at first but now finds the conversations more interesting.
quests.evidenceLine: Anwar's younger sister complained at first, but she now says that conversations are more interesting.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: The science teacher divided the class into three teams for a bridge-building competition. Each team had thirty sticks and a bottle of glue, and they had forty minutes to finish. The winning bridge was the one that held the most weight before collapsing. Team B's bridge held two kilograms, which was less than Team A's but more than Team C's. The teacher took photos of each bridge before the test began.
quests.question: Team C's bridge held more weight than Team B's.
quests.hint: Put the three teams in order of strength.
quests.explanation: Team B's bridge held more than Team C's, so the statement is reversed.
quests.evidenceLine: Team B's bridge held two kilograms, which was less than Team A's but more than Team C's.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Every year, the city holds a lottery to allocate places in its popular community gardens. Residents may apply for one plot, and each plot is about ten square meters. Those who win a place pay a small fee and must attend a short training session. Plots that are not used for a season are given to people on the waiting list. The waiting list currently has more than two hundred names.
quests.question: Residents can apply for several plots if they wish.
quests.hint: How many plots may one resident request?
quests.explanation: Residents may apply for one plot.
quests.evidenceLine: Residents may apply for one plot, and each plot is about ten square meters.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Ancient Egyptians used a calendar based on the yearly flooding of the Nile. The year had three seasons: flooding, planting, and harvest. Each season lasted four months, and each month had thirty days. Five extra days were added at the end to complete the year. Priests and farmers used the calendar to decide when to hold festivals.
quests.question: The Egyptian year was divided into four seasons.
quests.hint: Count the seasons in the passage.
quests.explanation: The year had three seasons, not four.
quests.evidenceLine: The year had three seasons: flooding, planting, and harvest.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully. Decide whether the statement is true or false according to the passage.
quests.passage: Cities are usually several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside, a phenomenon known as the urban heat island effect. Dark roofs and roads absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night. Planting trees and painting roofs white can lower temperatures noticeably. Some cities now require new buildings to include green roofs. Cool pavement materials are also being tested in several cities.
quests.question: Painting roofs white can help cool a city.
quests.hint: Look for the measures that lower temperatures.
quests.explanation: Planting trees and painting roofs white can lower temperatures noticeably.
quests.evidenceLine: Planting trees and painting roofs white can lower temperatures noticeably.
